'''Ama Kazukime Shrine''' (海士潜女神社, Ama Kazukime Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in {{ill|Kuzakichō|ja|国崎町|qid=Q11146786}}, {{ill|Toba, Mie|ar|توبا (ميه)|azb|توبا، میه|ce|Тоба (гӀала)|ceb|Toba-shi|ckb|تۆبا (میێ)|de|Toba (Mie)|eo|Toba (Mie)|es|Toba (Mie)|et|Toba|fa|توبا، میه|fi|Toba (Mie)|fr|Toba (Japon)|gl|Toba, Xapón|id|Toba, Mie|it|Toba|ja|鳥羽市|ko|도바시|mzn|توبا، میه|nl|Toba (stad)|pl|Toba (miasto)|pt|Toba (Mie)|ro|Toba, Japonia|ru|Тоба (город)|sr|Тоба Мије|sv|Toba (stad)|tg|Тоба|tl|Toba, Mie|tr|Toba (şehir)|tt|Тоба (шәһәр)|uk|Тоба (Міє)|ur|ٹوبا، میہ|uz|Toba (Mie)|vi|Toba, Mie|war|Toba, Mie|zh|鳥羽市|zh_classical|鳥羽市|zh_min_nan|Toba-chhī|zh_yue|鳥羽|qid=Q819629|lt=Toba City}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It was formerly known as Ama Gozen (海士御前) until 1869. While not under the administration of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}, it maintains a deep connection to Ise and enshrines the legendary {{ill|ama (female diver)|ja|海女|zh|海女|qid=Q15900642|lt=Ama diver}} Oben, attracting faith from divers across Japan.
Ama Kazukime Shrine enshrines the legendary ama named Oben, who dedicated an abalone to Emperor's Princess, Yamatohime-no-mikoto. The shrine is regarded as having divine favor in preventing dizziness during diving and is worshiped by local amas and divers nation-wide.<ref>https://www.bing.com/ck/a?!&&p=5de8780f388380bac94109889b3b4851fbe31c06bec1a4e2bc67168448801156JmltdHM9MTc0MzYzODQwMA&ptn=3&ver=2&hsh=4&fclid=0baff627-1adb-6b49-298a-e3e31b796a0d&u=a1aHR0cHM6Ly9xcnRyYW5zbGF0b3IuY29tLzAwMDAwMDE3NDcvMDAwMDAx&ntb=1</ref>
== Overview ==
The {{ill|Honden|en|Honden|qid=Q2044994|lt=honden}} of the shrine is a wooden structure in {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}}, while the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|es|Haiden (sintoísmo)|fa|هایدن (شینتو)|fi|Haiden|fr|Haiden|id|Haiden (Shinto)|it|Haiden|ja|拝殿|mk|Хаиден (Шинто)|pl|Haiden|pt|Haiden|ru|Хайдэн|tr|Haiden (Şinto)|qid=Q3125745|lt=haiden}} is built in {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} and surrounded by {{ill|sacred fences|ja|瑞垣}}. The grounds span approximately 920 {{ill|Pyeong|en|Pyeong|qid=Q706688|lt=tsubo}} (about 3,041 square meters). The main deity is Kazukime-no-Kami, identified with the legendary ama Oben. She is revered as the progenitor of ama divers, offering protection against dizziness and marine hazards. The shrine is also a pilgrimage site for divers across Japan.
== History ==
In the 26th year of Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Suinin}} (4 BCE), {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} visited Kuzaki while searching for offerings for the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. Oben presented abalone, which impressed Yamatohime and was subsequently dedicated to Ise. This marked Kuzaki’s selection as one of Ise’s {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Divine rice fields}}. The shrine was renamed Ama Kazukime Shrine in 1869 and later consolidated 17 smaller shrines between 1906 and 1907.
== Rituals ==
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally the festival of Hachiman Shrine, it centers around archery rituals held on {{ill|January 5|en|January 5|qid=Q2202|lt=January 5}}. Key rituals include the "Manabashi" ceremony, where chosen men prepare fish with chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.
=== Two Boat Festival ===
Held annually over three days in November, this festival involves competitive boat races between the Kuzaki subregions of Satodani and Kaimadani. Participants offer fish and {{ill|Omiki|en|Omiki|qid=Q3313722|lt=omiki}} at the {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} during the race, believed to predict the year’s fishing fortune.
=== Mikazuki Ritual and Grand Festival===
Historically, this ritual involved female divers from seven villages gathering on the lunar calendar's June 1 to dive for abalone. Although discontinued in 1871, the ritual has been periodically revived for commemorative occasions, such as the 2016 G7 Ise-Shima Summit.

== Subsidiary Shrines Enshrined Together ==
The Amamochime Shrine enshrines the following 17 shrines, which were merged into it in 1906 and 1907. === Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine ===
Tsurugi-no-Miya Shrine (剱宮社) was originally located on Tsurugi Cape. It was merged into Amamochime Shrine in 1906 (Meiji 39). It is also known simply as Tsurugi Shrine.<ref name="kk4"/> According to legend, one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|en|Imperial Regalia of Japan|qid=Q327465|lt=Three Sacred Treasures}}, the {{ill|Kusanagi no Tsurugi|ja|草薙剣|lt=Kusanagi Sword}}, which sank during the {{ill|Battle of Dan-no-ura|ar|معركة دان نو أورا|azb|دان نو اورا دؤیوشو|ca|Batalla de Dan-no-ura|cs|Bitva u Dannoury|de|Seeschlacht von Dan-no-ura|es|Batalla de Dan-no-ura|fa|نبرد دان نو اورا|fr|Bataille de Dan-no-ura|id|Pertempuran Dan-no-ura|it|Battaglia di Dan-no-ura|ja|壇ノ浦の戦い|ko|단노우라 전투|nl|Zeeslag bij Dan-no-ura|pl|Bitwa w zatoce Dan-no-Ura|pt|Batalha de Dan no Ura|ru|Битва при Данноуре|sv|Slaget vid Dan-no-ura|th|ยุทธนาวีที่ดันโนะอูระ|tr|Dan-no-ura Muharebesi|uk|Битва при Данноура|vi|Trận Dan no Ura|zh|壇之浦之戰|qid=Q968676|lt=Battle of Dan-no-ura}} alongside Emperor Antoku, was retrieved from the sea by a monk named Ajari Enjo and subsequently enshrined there.<ref name="kk4"/>
== Festivals ==
Amamochime Shrine is home to two major festivals in Kunisaki Town: the Hachiman Festival and the Two Boats Festival.<ref name="sg63">Shimamoto (1994): p. 163.</ref>
=== Hachiman Festival ===
Originally dedicated to the Hachiman Shrine, this festival centers around an archery ritual held on January 5th.<ref name="sg63"/> Hachiman Festivals are widely celebrated in fishing villages across Toba City, emphasizing prayers for bountiful catches and maritime safety.<ref>Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref> 
The festival includes:
* '''"Hatsuyori" (January 2nd):''' Preparatory meetings for the archery ritual.<ref name="sg63"/>
* '''"Daikon Kaki" (January 4th):''' Households prepare the offerings for the next day.<ref name="sg63"/>
During the festival, participants perform the {{ill|Manabashi Ritual|ja|真名箸神事}}, in which fish is filleted into sashimi using chopsticks and knives without touching it by hand.<ref name="th9">Toba City History Compilation Office (1991): p. 809.</ref>
=== Two Boats Festival ===
The Two Boats Festival (二船祭) takes place over three days in November.<ref name="tt">Toba Tourism Association "[http://www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Two Boats Festival]" <[https://megalodon.jp/2013-0421-1742-58/www.toba.gr.jp/200/post_523.html Web Archive]> (accessed April 21, 2013).</ref> The highlight is a boat race between the Kaima and Satodani communities, representing prayers for abundant fish catches.<ref name="sg63"/> 
== Surroundings ==
The shrine is located in Kunisaki Town, near the center of Toba City. Visitors can take the Kamome Bus from the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=JR Sangu Line}} Toba Station to the Kunisaki stop, followed by a 7-minute walk.<ref name="cv"/> Note that there is no dedicated parking space nearby.<ref name="cv"/>
